The Rényi divergence is defined as $D_\alpha(P || Q) = \frac{1}{\alpha - 1} \log E_{Y \sim Q} \left[ \left(\frac{P(Y)}{Q(Y)}\right)^\alpha \right]$.

The $L_2$-sensitivity of $f$ is defined as $\Delta_2 f = \max_{X, X' \text{ adjacent}} |f(X) - f(X')|$.

$|f(X) - f(X')| = \left| \sum_{i=1}^n \left| x_i - \frac{i}{n} \right| - \sum_{i=1}^n \left| x_i' - \frac{i}{n} \right| \right|$

$|f(X) - f(X')| = \left| \left| x_j - \frac{j}{n} \right| - \left| x_j' - \frac{j}{n} \right| \right|$
Using the reverse triangle inequality, which states that $||a|-|b|| \le |a-b|$, we can write:
$\left| \left| x_j - \frac{j}{n} \right| - \left| x_j' - \frac{j}{n} \right| \right| \le \left| \left( x_j - \frac{j}{n} \right) - \left( x_j' - \frac{j}{n} \right) \right| = |x_j - x_j'|$
Since $x_j, x_j' \in [0, 1]$, the maximum possible value for $|x_j - x_j'|$ is $1-0 = 1$.
Therefore, the $L_2$-sensitivity of $f(X)$ is $\Delta_2 f = 1$.
